sentences.text:
2024 
 1
 The Honourable Sri Justice E.V.Venugopal
 Criminal Revision Case No.894 Of 2024
Order:

The Criminal Revision Case is filed aggrieved by the order dated 17.05.2024 in Crl.M.P.No.1380 of 2022 in C.C.No.17.05.2024 on the file of the learned Judicial First Class Magistrate at Choutuppal (for short, "the trial Court") seeking to discharge the petitioner/accused No.2 from the charges under Sections 417, 420, 203, 120(B) r/w 34 of Indian Penal Code.
2.

entities.text: Judicial First Class Magistrate at Choutuppal
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Heard M.A.K.Mujkheed, learned counsel for the petitioner/accused No.2 and Sri Jithender Rao Veeramalla, learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the respondent No.1- State.
3. The brief facts of the case are that on 03.11.2020 at about 12.00 hours while the son of LW.1 and his friend were proceeding to Hyderabad from Guntur on Honda Activa bike bearing No.AP 39 R 6453.

On the way at about 22.00 hours, when they reached Dharmojigudem "X" road of Chotuppal Mandal, meantime, the offending vehicle, which is car bearing No.TS08 FL 7001, driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner and dashed LW.1 son's bike from rear side, due to which the son of LW.1 died on the spot.
Basing on the said facts, F.I.R.No.442 of 2020 was registered against accused Nos.1 to 3 for the offences punishable under Sections 419, 420, 203, 120(B) r/w 34 of IPC.
Petitioner/accused No.2 filed a discharge application before the trial Court, seeking to discharge him from the charges levelled against him.
The trial Court, vide impugned order, dismissed the discharge application filed by petitioner/accused No.2, stating that there are sufficient grounds to proceed against the petitioner.
Assailing the same, the petitioner filed the present Revision.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the trial Court had passed the impugned order,
in a mechanical manner, without applying its judicious mind to the facts of the case.
He further stated that charges were framed against the petitioner and thereupon, trial is continuing curtailing the right of the petitioner.
Therefore, he seeks to allow the Revision.
5. Opposing the same, learned counsel for unofficial respondent No.2 contended that all the witnesses have been examined and nothing remains so far.
Therefore, he stated that interference of this Court, at this stage, is not warranted and seeks to dismiss this Revision.

6. Having regard to the submissions made by both the learned counsel and without making any observations on the merits or demerits of this case, this Court deems it appropriate to direct the trial Court to conduct and conclude the trial, as expeditiously as possible, preferably, within a period of Thaduru Paramesh vs The State Of Telangana on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/103777860/
1 six (6) months from today.
7.

entities.text: Thaduru Paramesh vs The State Of Telangana
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: With the above direction, this Criminal Revision Case is disposed of.
However, the presence of the petitioner/accused No.2 in the subject Calendar Case, before the trial Court, is dispensed with on each and every adjournment unless and until specifically required.
Miscellaneous Petitions, pending if any, shall stand closed.

E.V. VENUGOPAL, J Date: 11.11.2024 mmr Thaduru Paramesh vs The State Of Telangana on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/103777860/
